summary: Well-executed, preregistered paired study comparing a baseline single‑shot LLM generator to a guarded generate→validate→repair pipeline under shared_initial_candidate semantics. Experiment execution, archiving, and analysis are complete and internally consistent. Primary confirmatory test (exact two‑sided McNemar) did not meet α=0.05 (p=0.0625); bootstrap CI reported as preregistered secondary descriptive summary. Major methodological choices (shared_initial_candidate, deterministic validator, repair budget) and limitations are disclosed.
critical_issues: None that invalidate the scientific record. The preregistered design, execution manifest, and archived artifacts support the reported confirmatory analysis and the manuscript appropriately bounds conclusions given the nonsignificant primary test and sparse discordant counts.
required_revisions: Provide a conventional IEEE‑style References section (numbered bibliography entries with authors, title, venue, year) rather than identifier‑only entries so each in‑text numeric citation is resolvable to full bibliographic metadata.

Condense the Disclosure Statement to remove near‑verbatim execution logs and per‑file bookkeeping while preserving the mandatory immutable master_prompt locator and its SHA‑256 digest verbatim. The Disclosure should remain within pages 1–5 and avoid duplicating analysis/execution artifacts already archived.

Explicitly confirm in Methods that shared_initial_candidate semantics entailed exactly one sampled initial generation per task reused across both arms (i.e., no independent first‑pass generations were performed), and point readers to the archived provider_call accounting (execution/model_configuration.json and deterministic_reconciliation.json) for the recorded sampling parameters (temperature=null) and host‑call counts. (This can be satisfied by adding one concise statement and an archival pointer; no new model calls are required.)
optional_revisions: As a sensitivity disclosure, add the one‑sided exact McNemar p‑value (directional test consistent with H1) computed from the archived contingency table and label it clearly as a sensitivity, not the preregistered primary two‑sided inferential result (no new experiments required; contingency table is archived).

Briefly expand the Threats to Validity section to discuss validator coverage/permissiveness (how validator rule set could inflate baseline success) using archived validator trace examples (already archived) as illustrative evidence, without adding new analyses.
Consider reporting the exact numeric sampling/temperature fields from execution/model_configuration.json (already archived) inline to avoid reader inference about null/unset sampling semantics.
